findings.title: Code injection via eval() on textarea content
findings.explanation: renderJson() builds the JSON payload to render by calling eval('(' + $('#json-input').val() + ')') instead of JSON.parse(). Any text placed in the #json-input textarea is executed as arbitrary JavaScript in the page's origin rather than merely parsed as data. Because the textarea is rendered on page load with attacker-influenceable content in any scenario where this demo page is embedded, pre-filled from another page/extension, or where a user is persuaded to paste untrusted 'JSON' text and click 'Transform to HTML', this acts as a direct eval-injection sink. The fix is to use JSON.parse() (or a safe JSON5 parser) which cannot execute arbitrary statements.
